vilayet_stats.source: Muslims: Tuna gazette 1873 with the Rusçuk 'tetimme', 220,718 Muslim males. This equals Aubaret's Ottoman-based 441,000 (388,000 Turks, 33,000 Circassians, 20,000 Muslim Roma). Non-Muslims: 119,179 males (Tahrir-i Cedid 1874: 119,175; Bulgarians 114,792 = 37.05%), x2, minus 1,102 Jewish males. Kaza split from the 1290/1873 salname (Koyuncu 2014, Tables 12 and 15). Both sexes, Jews excluded.

1290/1873 Tuna salname, corrected (Koyuncu 2014, Table 12): 37,195 Muslim / 156,486 non-Muslim males, x2. Added: Circassians documented but not registered in Adliye (~3,000) and İvraca (~1,100), plus 3,554 to reach Aubaret's upper bound (69,000 Muslims excluding Circassians, plus 13,044 Circassians from the TC). TC 1874 (1292 salname): 29,797 Muslim / 149,026 non-Muslim males; Bulgarians 73.41%; 'Ulah, Katolik vs.' 14,690 males. Jews (1,009 males) excluded.

vilayet_stats.vilayet: Tuna Vilayeti – Sofya sancağı (excl. Cuma-i Bâlâ)
vilayet_stats.source: TC 1874: 30,167 Muslim / 183,013 non-Muslim males for the whole sancak (Bulgarians 84.06%; Jews 2,374; Christian Roma 1,437). Kaza shares from the 1290/1873 salname. Cuma-i Bâlâ kaza (~3,570 M / 9,590 N males) is left to the Macedonian region. Added 3,000 Circassian males: Koyuncu shows that 20,000 muhacirs were dropped from the 1292 salname, Sofya among them. Jews excluded.

TC 1874: 94,990 Muslim / 150,904 non-Muslim males (Bulgarians 148,713 = 60.48%; no Jews). Kaza and nahiye split from the 1290/1873 salname (75,387 / 116,810). Added 5,000 Circassian males: Koyuncu notes that no Circassians were registered in Tırnova although they were present (part of the 20,000 omitted).

TC 1874: 59,874 Muslim / 25,931 non-Muslim males (Bulgarians 24.78%, Gagauz included among them; Greeks 3,421; Armenians 808; Circassians 4,307; Jews 110). Kaza split from the 1290 salname, corrected, plus 675 Pravadi town Muslims. Pazarcık non-Muslims kept at the 1873 value of 3,381 (local defters: 2,504-2,549). Added 7,000 omitted Circassian males (Koyuncu). Jews excluded.

1290/1873 salname, corrected (Koyuncu 2014, Table 12): 67,331 Muslim / 44,163 non-Muslim males, x2, minus 780 Jewish males. Preferred over TC 1874 (56,152 / 31,303), which Koyuncu shows is incomplete for Tulça. Cross-check: the 1878 estimate for N. Dobruja is 225,692.

vilayet_stats.year: 1873 register; Muslims raised to McCarthy's 1876 figure
vilayet_stats.source: 1873 Ottoman register (Prizren vilayet salname, via Jagodić 1998, Table 1), males Muslim / Christian: Niş 4,291 / 17,107; Şehirköy 5,772 / 29,741; Leskofça 10,525 / 21,030; Ürgüp 6,207 / 4,618; Kurşunlu 5,951 / 757; Turan 149 / 7,072. Muslims x2 x1.423, scaled to McCarthy's 131,000 Muslims for the sancak in 1876. Christians x2 x1.03 (Jagodić's 1873-77 growth). Vranje kaza excluded. The 1877 Ottoman count for the same area minus Vranje was 237,055.

vilayet_stats.vilayet: Tuna Vilayeti – whole region (7 sancaks as above)
vilayet_stats.source: Sum of the sancak rows: both sexes, Jews excluded, Cuma-i Bâlâ and Vranje excluded. Official reference: TC 1874 total 1,141,051 males (Tuna gazette, Koyuncu Table 18; Muslims 481,798 = 42.2%), x2 = 2,282,102 without Niş. Koyuncu's 1874 total with Niş is 2,594,928 (40.7% Muslim).

sources: Aşkın Koyuncu, 'Tuna Vilâyeti'nde Nüfus ve Demografi (1864-1877)', Turkish Studies 9/4 (2014), 675-737, doi:10.7827/TurkishStudies.7023 (full text: https://turkishstudies.net/files/turkishstudies/880266314_38KoyuncuAşkın-trh-675-737.pdf). Main source. Used for: Table 12 (1290/1873 Tuna salname, corrected kaza male counts); Table 13 and its text (1873 urban Muslim % for every town); Table 15 (Tuna gazette 1873, incl. the Rusçuk 'tetimme' and the new tahrir for Silistre and Tutrakan); Tables 18-21 (Tahrir-i Cedid 1874 in the Tuna gazette and the 1292/1875 salname: sancak Muslim/Circassian/Roma/Bulgarian/Greek/Vlach/Jewish counts; the 20,000 muhacirs omitted from the salname; Bulgarian share by sancak); the muhacir village lists for Vidin, Adliye, Lom, Rahova, Berkofça, İvraca and Plevne; Gözler's 40 Pomak villages; the Pazarcık defters (NBKM); and Aubaret's Rusçuk and Vidin figures (via E. D. Tanır).

Salnâme-i Vilâyet-i Tuna, Defa 6 (1290/1873), Defa 7 (1291/1874), Defa 8 (1292/1875). Used as transcribed and corrected by Koyuncu. The 1291 printing errors (Sofya columns swapped, Osman Pazarı swapped, Rahova/Belgradçık mixed up) were not used uncorrected.
TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi, 'Hezargrad' (https://islamansiklopedisi.org.tr/hezargrad): Hezargrad town in 1873 had 10,400 people (6,860 Muslim, 3,540 non-Muslim).

Miloš Jagodić, 'The Emigration of Muslims from the New Serbian Regions 1877/1878', Balkanologie II/2 (1998), Table 1: the 1873 Ottoman (Prizren vilayet salname) male counts by kaza for the Niş sancak, Muslim/Christian houses in towns, language of the urban Muslims, and the 1877 Ottoman count of the Niş and Pirot sancaks (237,055).

Justin McCarthy, 'Muslims in Ottoman Europe: Population from 1800-1912', Nationalities Papers 28/1 (2000), p. 35: 131,000 Muslims in the Niş sancak in 1876 (as cited in Wikipedia, 'Expulsion of the Albanians 1877-1878'). Used as the upper-end Turk-friendly figure.
Kemal H. Karpat, 'Ottoman Population 1830-1914' (1985), pp. 156-157, and Ömer Turan, as compared and corrected by Koyuncu (Koyuncu shows Karpat's 1291/1874 totals carry the salname's misprints).

Nikolai Todorov, 'The Balkan City 1400-1900' (1983), as cited by Koyuncu: Greeks were partly registered as Bulgarians (Varna: 3,532 Greek vs 662 Bulgarian taxpayers). Used for the non-Bulgarian Christian share in Varna and Balçık.
Carl Sax, 'Ethnographische Karte der europäischen Türkei' (1878), via the earlier research pass. Used only for where each group lived inside a kaza (source policy step 3).
geoBoundaries BGR ADM1 (Bulgarian oblasts, 2019) for the oblast calibration check, and Natural Earth 10m land/lakes to check that every cluster centre is on land.
caveats: CALIBRATION AGAINST THE USER'S 1875 OBLAST TARGETS. Bulgarian % is computed on cluster centres inside each modern oblast, with Jews put back into the denominator and Gagauz, Greeks, Armenians, Vlachs and Christian Roma treated as non-Bulgarian. Within ±5: Ruse 36.3 (target 38), Silistra 26.4 (27), Varna 27.0 (25), Veliko Tarnovo 62.7 (60), Pleven 54.5 (58), Vratsa 75.4 (76), Montana 79.8 (75), Sofia oblast 83.4 (86), Pernik 90.3 (90), Kyustendil 83.8 (88), Sofia city 41.5 (42; the town of Sofia alone). NOT within ±5: Razgrad 12.3 (37), Shumen 20.1 (43), Targovishte 24.0 (40), Lovech 52.8 (76), Gabrovo 80.1 (93), Vidin 53.0 (73), Dobrich 17.8 (25). In every one of these the Ottoman records show MORE non-Bulgarians than the target.

WHY THESE SEVEN DO NOT MATCH. The user's oblast figures reproduce the 1874 Tahrir-i Cedid Bulgarian share of each whole sancak (1292 salname, Koyuncu Table 20: Vidin 73.41, Tırnova 60.48, Varna 24.78, Rusçuk 37.05, Sofya 84.06), spread evenly over every oblast of the sancak. The 1290/1873 salname kaza figures show the Muslims concentrated in particular kazas: Hezargrad 73% Muslim, Şumnu 74%, Cuma-i Atik 81%, Osman Pazarı 91%, Lofça 58% (incl. Pomaks), Servi 40%, Vidin kaza 41%. Vidin oblast also holds most of the ~29,000 Vlachs ('Ulah, Katolik vs.' 14,690 males). Reaching the targets in these oblasts would mean cutting Muslim numbers below the Ottoman registers, which the source policy (Ottoman figures first, never invent) does not allow. The salname kaza figures were therefore kept. At sancak level the dataset matches the Tahrir-i Cedid within about 4 points: Bulgarian share Rusçuk 33.1 (TC 37.05; Aubaret 33.8), Tırnova 59.3 (60.48), Vidin 71.0 (73.41), Sofya 82.8 (84.06), Varna 21.2 (24.78), Tulça 10.7 (12.07). The author may prefer to override this choice for the seven oblasts.

Dobrich and Varna: the Tahrir-i Cedid counted Gagauz (and some Greeks) as 'Bulgar'. The user's definition counts them as non-Bulgarian. Counted the Ottoman way, Dobrich would be about 21-22% Bulgarian.

Sofia city: the modern 'Sofia City' oblast polygon also contains the Sofia-plain villages, which were about 87-95% Bulgarian, so the whole polygon comes out at 77%. The target of 42% only fits the town itself: 15,000 non-Jews at 47% Muslim (1873 urban figure), plus about 3,400 Jews.
Sliven, Burgas and Blagoevgrad targets lie mostly in the Edirne and Selanik regions. Only Kotel (Kazgan nahiye, Sliven oblast, 87.5% Bulgarian) is in this dataset.

Populations are 1873/74 male counts x2 (both sexes), with documented corrections added: Rusçuk sancak raised to the Tuna-gazette/Aubaret Muslim total; Circassians omitted from the 1292 salname put back (7,000 males Varna, 5,000 Tırnova, 3,000 Sofya, split by me, out of Koyuncu's 20,000; Tulça's share is covered by using the higher 1873 figures); unregistered Circassians in Adliye and İvraca; Niş Muslims raised to McCarthy's 1876 figure. No natural growth was added for 1874-76, except the 3% Jagodić applies to Niş Christians.

Rusçuk sancak: how the 37,055 extra Muslim males are split by kaza is my assumption. The total is sourced (Tuna gazette 1873 tetimme = Aubaret 441,000), and so are the 16,588 Circassians (TC 1874) and Koyuncu's remark that Plevne's 27 villages had no Muslim figures. The split was: Plevne +6,000 for those villages and the 1861 muhacir villages; Circassians Rusçuk 4,500, Hezargrad 2,500, Şumnu 2,500, Niğbolu 2,500, Plevne 2,588, Ziştovi 2,000; the remaining 14,467 in proportion to 1873 Muslims in the kazas the 1873 tahrir had not re-counted.

Some kaza assignments are uncertain, which affects which oblast the population falls in: the Popovo/Opaka area (put in Hezargrad), Lukovit–Cherven Bryag–Roman (İvraca), Teteven and Etropol (Orhaniye), Kamçı/Emine (Varna kaza), Luda Kamçı (Pravadi), Belene (Ziştovi), the Iskar mouth (Niğbolu), Levski–Letnitsa (Plevne), the Kara Harman coast (Babadağı), Tekirgöl (Köstence), Cernavodă (Hırsova).

Town populations are estimates scaled from the 1873 urban male counts and the 1880-81 censuses (Hezargrad's 10,400 is from TDV). Town Muslim shares are Koyuncu's 1873 urban percentages, converted to a non-Jewish basis.

Within each kaza, the village clusters keep the draft's spatial pattern (from Sax). One uniform shift in Muslim odds was applied so that each kaza's total equals the Ottoman figure. The village-cluster shares are therefore only as precise as the draft's internal pattern.

Varna kaza: the TC added 54% more non-Muslims than 1873 (Greeks and Gagauz; Todorov). With Varna town fixed at its 1873 share of 67.7% Muslim, the Varna villages come out at only 40-43% Muslim. If the increase was really urban Greeks, the town would be less Muslim and the villages more.

Köstence kaza had only 301 non-Muslim males in the 1290 salname, so its villages are about 99-100% Muslim. Sax's Bulgarian coastal villages north of Köstence sit in the Kara Harman cluster (Babadağı kaza).

Niş: the McCarthy correction raises Muslims only. As a result the Niş total (259,000) is about 9% above the 1877 Ottoman count for the same area (237,055), and the rural Albanian clusters (Pusta Reka, Toplica, Kosanica) reach 75-92% Muslim.

Turk vs muslim_other: Tatars and Nogais count as turk; Circassians, Pomaks, Muslim Roma and Albanian-speaking Muslims as muslim_other. Sancak checks: Rusçuk 87% Turk (Aubaret 388,000 of 441,000), Varna 81%, Tırnova 77%, Sofya 80.5%, Vidin 61%, Tulça 92%, Niş 21%.

Excluded: Jews (about 11,000: Sofya ~4,750, Rusçuk ~2,200, Vidin ~2,000, Tulça ~1,560, Varna ~220), Cuma-i Bâlâ kaza (Sofya sancak, Blagoevgrad area) and Vranje kaza (Niş sancak). Neighbouring regions must cover the last two.
changes: Added a population to all 138 clusters, derived from Ottoman kaza totals (1873/74 male counts x2 plus documented corrections). Cluster populations within each kaza add up exactly to that kaza's total, and sancak totals equal the vilayet_stats rows. Region total: 2,639,581 non-Jewish people.

Rusçuk sancak Muslims raised from the Tahrir-i Cedid's 190,622 males to 220,718 males (Tuna gazette 1873 with 'tetimme' = Aubaret 441,000 both sexes; Koyuncu says the TC is ~30,000 Muslim males short). As a result: Rusçuk villages rose 8-10 points (Vetovo–Senovo 68→76% Muslim, Byala 36→45%, Slivo Pole 48→58%); Plevne villages rose (N/W 42→52%, Pomak–Tatar south 55→65%, Levski 29→38%) because of the 27 villages registered without Muslim figures and the 1861 muhacir villages (Koyuncu); Ziştovi villages 40→54% (Tatar/Circassian colonies).

Town clusters set to Koyuncu's 1873 urban Muslim shares (non-Jewish basis): Plevne 49→44, Vidin 56→60, Sofya 54→47 (39.16% of all males incl. Jews), Varna 63→67.7, Köstence 81→88, Hırsova 66→73, Tutrakan 44→42.5, Ziştovi 40→37.5, Tırnova 32→35.6. Hezargrad stays at 66, matching TDV 1873 (6,860 M / 3,540 N).

Lofça kaza re-weighted to the 1290 salname (21,508 Muslim vs 15,397 non-Muslim males = 58%): Lofça NW Pomak villages 73→84% Muslim, Ugarçin–Yablanitsa Pomaks 48→64%, Osam villages 47→63%. Pomaks are muslim_other, following Gözler's 40 Pomak villages (26,990 Muslims in 1873).

Silistre kaza set to its new-tahrir figure (Tuna gazette 1873: 35,616 M / 16,782 N males = 68% Muslim): Danube villages 55→41%, Kalipetrovo 66→52%, Dulovo 93→88%, Tervel 90→84%, Romanian-side Dobruja 75→63%. The draft was above the Ottoman figure here.

Hezargrad kaza set to the corrected 1290 figure plus its share of the Circassians and new-tahrir increment (77% Muslim): Deliorman 93→90%, Kostandenets 56→47%, Bela–Opaka 61→52%. Şumnu kaza (salname 35,657 M, preferred over the gazette's 30,652, which Koyuncu calls an implausible drop): Preslav 63→70%, Yeni Pazar 82→86%. Eski Cuma villages 84→90%, Osman Pazarı 91→93% (1290: 90.7%).

Vidin sancak: 1290 salname kaza totals plus documented unregistered Circassians (Adliye ~3,000, İvraca ~1,100; Koyuncu), plus Aubaret's upper bound (+3,554 in Lom and Berkofça). Lom muhacir belt 16→25% Muslim, Rahova W 25→35%, Rahova S 14→21%, Vidin S 36→41%, Belgradçık 17→20%. Named Circassian and Tatar muhacir villages from the salname added to the group descriptions. Vlachs ('Ulah, Katolik vs.' 14,690 males) are concentrated in Vidin, Adliye and Lom.

Varna sancak: kaza totals scaled to TC 1874, with 7,000 omitted Circassian males added. The Turk share of Muslims was lowered to ~81% (TC: 52,742 İslam vs 4,307 Circassians + 2,825 Muslim Roma, plus the omitted Circassians), giving Pazarcık clusters muslim_other 17-22% (Pazarcık defter: 8,211-9,150 Tatar–Circassian muhacirs). Varna villages fell 60→40-43% Muslim, because the 1874 count added many non-Muslims.

Tulça sancak: uses the corrected 1290 salname (Babadağı 15,706 Muslims instead of the misprinted 4,756). Köstence villages 93-95→99.5%, Hırsova inner and north 75-85→84-91%, Cernavodă 56→69%, Mahmudiye 53→59%, Tulça town 23→18%.

Sofya sancak: kaza totals scaled to TC 1874, with 3,000 Circassian males added (2,000 in Sofya kaza, mainly the Slivnitsa / Niš-road cluster, 7→21% Muslim; 500 Radomir; 500 Köstendil). Sofia plain 7→13%. Köstendil town and environs 27→21%, Orhaniye 13→9%, Etropol 29→21% (Orhaniye kaza was 10.5% Muslim in 1873). Teteven Pomaks 19→13%.

Niş sancak: Muslims raised from the 1873 register (32,895 males excl. Vranje) to McCarthy's 1876 level (x1.42). Pusta Reka 72→93% Muslim, Leskovac W 43→78%, Toplica 60→75%, Prokuplje N 20→34%, Leskovac E 3→13%, Niš villages 7→12%. Prokuplje town re-labelled Albanian-speaking (Jagodić), turk 33→12.

Turk vs muslim_other calibrated to the Ottoman categories for each sancak: Rusçuk 87% Turk (Aubaret), Tırnova 77%, Vidin 61%, Sofya 80.5%, Tulça 92%, Niş 21%. Kazgan (Kotel) and Gabrova Muslims moved fully to muslim_other (the salname notes they were Roma). Elena and Tryavna set to 0 Muslims (salname).

Added the vilayet field ('Tuna') and the 1876 sancak to every cluster. Osman Pazarı, Vırbiçe and Kazgan are in Tırnova sancak; Mankalya, Pazarcık, Balçık and Pravadi in Varna sancak; Köstence, Mecidiye, Hırsova and Babadağı in Tulça sancak. All coordinates were checked on land against Natural Earth. Nothing was moved.
